points.title: 童年与少年时期
points.description: 1879年3月14日，爱因斯坦出生于德国巴登-符腾堡州乌尔姆市的一个犹太中产阶级家庭。1880年全家迁居慕尼黑，父亲和叔叔在那里经营一家电气设备公司。童年时期的爱因斯坦展现出对自然现象的强烈好奇心，但对传统教育方式感到厌倦。1894年，父亲生意失败，全家移居意大利米兰，但爱因斯坦被留在德国完成中学学业。这段时期他自学了高等数学和物理，并开始质疑当时物理学的基础理论。
points.descriptionEn: Born on March 14, 1879, in Ulm, Germany, to a middle-class Jewish family, Einstein showed early signs of curiosity about natural phenomena but struggled with traditional education methods. In 1880, his family moved to Munich where his father and uncle ran an electrical equipment business. By 1894, the business failed and the family relocated to Milan, Italy, leaving Einstein behind to complete his secondary education in Germany. During this period, he self-studied advanced mathematics and physics, beginning to question the fundamental theories of contemporary physics.

points.title: 求学与早期研究
points.description: 1896年，爱因斯坦进入苏黎世联邦理工学院（ETH）学习物理和数学。虽然他在数学上表现出色，但在物理实验课上表现平平。在此期间，他结识了同学米列娃·马里奇，后来成为他的第一任妻子。1900年，爱因斯坦毕业，但未能立即获得学术职位，只能在瑞士专利局担任技术员工作。这段看似平凡的专利局工作反而给了他大量时间思考物理学问题，为后来的革命性发现奠定了基础。
points.descriptionEn: In 1896, Einstein enrolled at the Swiss Federal Polytechnic (ETH) in Zurich to study physics and mathematics. While excelling in mathematics, he performed poorly in physics laboratory courses. During this time, he met fellow student Mileva Marić, who later became his first wife. Einstein graduated in 1900 but struggled to secure an academic position, eventually working as a patent clerk at the Swiss Patent Office. This seemingly mundane job ironically provided him with ample time to contemplate physics problems, laying the foundation for his later revolutionary discoveries.

points.title: 奇迹之年
points.description: 1905年被称为爱因斯坦的'奇迹之年'，他在瑞士专利局工作期间发表了四篇划时代的论文，彻底改变了物理学界。这四篇论文分别解释了光电效应（为量子理论奠定基础）、布朗运动（提供了原子存在的证据）、狭义相对论（革新了时空观念）以及质能等价（E=mc²）。这些成就使他在科学界崭露头角，1908年获得伯尔尼大学讲师职位，1909年升任苏黎世大学教授。1911年，他提出光线在引力场中弯曲的预言，1913年接受柏林威廉皇帝物理研究所所长职位，准备返回德国。
points.descriptionEn: 1905, known as Einstein's 'Annus Mirabilis,' saw him publish four groundbreaking papers while working at the Swiss Patent Office that revolutionized physics. These papers explained the photoelectric effect (laying foundation for quantum theory), Brownian motion (providing evidence for atomic existence), special relativity (revolutionizing concepts of space and time), and mass-energy equivalence (E=mc²). These achievements brought Einstein to prominence in scientific circles, earning him a lectureship at the University of Bern in 1908 and a professorship at the University of Zurich in 1909. In 1911, he predicted that light would bend in gravitational fields, and in 1913, he accepted the position of director at the Kaiser Wilhelm Institute for Physics in Berlin, preparing to return to Germany.

points.title: 科学巅峰与政治觉醒
points.description: 1914年，爱因斯坦移居柏林，开始了他在科学和政治上的重要时期。1915年，他完成了广义相对论的建立，这是对牛顿引力理论的彻底革新。1919年，英国天文学家爱丁顿通过日食观测证实了爱因斯坦关于光线弯曲的预言，使他一夜之间成为国际名人。1921年，他因光电效应的研究获得诺贝尔物理学奖。随着纳粹在德国的崛起，爱因斯坦作为犹太人和和平主义者成为攻击目标。1933年，希特勒上台后，爱因斯坦公开谴责纳粹政权，并宣布放弃德国国籍，返回美国。
points.descriptionEn: Moving to Berlin in 1914, Einstein entered a crucial period both scientifically and politically. In 1915, he completed his general theory of relativity, a complete revolution of Newton's theory of gravity. In 1919, British astronomer Arthur Eddington confirmed Einstein's prediction about light bending during a solar eclipse, making him an international overnight celebrity. In 1921, he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics for his work on the photoelectric effect. With the rise of Nazism in Germany, Einstein, as both a Jew and a pacifist, became a target of attacks. After Hitler came to power in 1933, Einstein publicly condemned the Nazi regime and renounced his German citizenship, returning to the United States.

points.title: 流亡岁月与核能时代
points.description: 1933年，爱因斯坦接受普林斯顿高等研究院的邀请移居美国，成为终身教授。尽管他本人是和平主义者，但在意识到纳粹德国可能研发原子弹的危险后，他在1939年致信罗斯福总统，建议美国也开展核研究。这封信直接促成了曼哈顿计划的启动。战后，爱因斯坦对核武器的出现深感忧虑，积极参与推动国际控制核能的运动。1940年，他成为美国公民。在普林斯顿期间，他致力于统一场论的研究，试图将引力与电磁力统一起来，但未能成功。这一时期也是他积极参与公民权利和和平运动的时期。
points.descriptionEn: In 1933, Einstein accepted an invitation to join the Institute for Advanced Study in Princeton, becoming a lifelong professor. Despite being a pacifist, he grew concerned about the possibility of Nazi Germany developing atomic weapons and wrote to President Roosevelt in 1939, suggesting the U.S. also pursue nuclear research. This letter directly led to the Manhattan Project. After the war, Einstein became deeply concerned about the emergence of nuclear weapons and actively advocated for international control of nuclear energy. In 1940, he became a U.S. citizen. During his Princeton years, he worked on developing a unified field theory, attempting to unify gravity and electromagnetism, though without success. This period also saw him actively involved in civil rights and peace movements.

points.title: 晚年与科学遗产
points.description: 二战后，爱因斯坦继续在普林斯顿工作，但逐渐将更多精力投入到和平主义和世界政府理念中。他发表了著名的《罗素-爱因斯坦宣言》，呼吁科学家关注核武器对人类文明的威胁。1952年，以色列邀请他担任第二任总统，但他婉拒了这一政治职位。1955年4月18日，爱因斯坦因主动脉瘤破裂在普林斯顿医院逝世，享年76岁。临终前，他仍在继续统一场论的研究。爱因斯坦的遗产远超物理学领域，他成为智慧、创新和人文关怀的象征，他的思想继续影响着科学、哲学和大众文化。
points.descriptionEn: After World War II, Einstein continued working in Princeton but gradually devoted more energy to pacifism and world government ideals. He co-authored the famous Russell-Einstein Manifesto, urging scientists to consider the threat of nuclear weapons to human civilization. In 1952, he was offered the presidency of Israel but declined this political position. On April 18, 1955, Einstein died at Princeton Hospital from an abdominal aortic aneurysm at age 76. He was still working on his unified field theory until his final days. Einstein's legacy extends far beyond physics; he has become a symbol of intelligence, innovation, and humanistic concern, and his ideas continue to influence science, philosophy, and popular culture.

appraisal.zh: 爱因斯坦被公认为20世纪最伟大的科学家之一，相对论彻底改变了人类对宇宙的理解，他也被视为科学探索精神的化身，并以和平与正义的倡导体现科学家的社会责任。不过他并非无懈可击：他在量子力学上的保守立场使他错失了参与这一领域革命的机会，对第一任妻子米列娃·马里奇在相对论研究中贡献的认可不足，在核武器问题上从建议美国研发到后来强烈反对的转变也被一些人视为政治机会主义，其统一场论则被批评为过于固守经典物理学的框架。学界如今更强调他的复杂性：他既是革命性的思想家，也是20世纪动荡历史的产物。
appraisal.en: Einstein is widely regarded as one of the greatest scientists of the 20th century, whose theories of relativity transformed humanity's understanding of the universe; he is also seen as the embodiment of scientific exploration and, through his advocacy of peace and justice, of the scientist's social responsibility. Yet he was not without flaws: his conservative stance on quantum mechanics cost him a part in that field's revolution, he gave insufficient recognition to Mileva Marić's contributions to his relativity research, and his shift from urging the U.S. to build atomic weapons to strongly opposing them has been read by some as political opportunism, while his unified field theory has been criticized as too bound to classical physics. Historians now stress his complexity—a revolutionary thinker and a product of his turbulent century.

supporter.zh: 爱因斯坦被誉为20世纪最伟大的科学家之一，他的相对论彻底改变了人类对宇宙的理解。支持者认为他代表了科学探索的最高精神，他的好奇心、想象力和批判性思维为后世科学家树立了典范。爱因斯坦不仅推动了科学革命，还积极倡导和平与正义，体现了科学家的社会责任感。他的名言'想象力比知识更重要'激励着无数创新者，而他对统一理论的追求则体现了科学探索的终极目标。
supporter.en: Einstein is celebrated as one of the greatest scientists of the 20th century, whose theories of relativity revolutionized humanity's understanding of the universe. Supporters view him as embodying the highest ideals of scientific exploration, with his curiosity, imagination, and critical thinking setting a standard for future generations. Beyond his scientific contributions, Einstein actively advocated for peace and justice, demonstrating the social responsibility of scientists. His famous quote 'Imagination is more important than knowledge' continues to inspire innovators, while his pursuit of a unified theory represents the ultimate goal of scientific inquiry.

critic.zh: 批评者指出爱因斯坦并非完美无缺。他在量子力学上的保守立场使他错失了参与这一领域革命的机会。他的个人生活也充满争议，包括对第一任妻子米列娃·马里奇在相对论研究中的贡献缺乏足够认可。此外，爱因斯坦在核武器问题上的立场前后矛盾，从最初建议美国研发原子弹到后来强烈反对核武器，被一些人视为政治机会主义。他的统一场论研究也被批评为过于执着于经典物理学的框架，未能充分接受量子力学的新范式。
critic.en: Critics point out that Einstein was not without flaws. His conservative stance on quantum mechanics caused him to miss opportunities to participate in that field's revolution. His personal life also contains controversies, including insufficient recognition of Mileva Marić's contributions to his relativity research. Additionally, Einstein's position on nuclear weapons appears contradictory—from initially advocating for the U.S. to develop atomic weapons to later strongly opposing them—leading some to view it as political opportunism. His unified field theory research has been criticized for being too attached to classical physics frameworks, failing to fully embrace the new paradigm of quantum mechanics.

objective.zh: 在历史学和流行文化中，爱因斯坦已成为超越科学领域的文化符号。他被广泛视为天才的化身，其形象经常被用来代表智慧和创造力。爱因斯坦的相对论不仅是科学成就，也成为哲学思考的源泉，挑战了人们对时间、空间和现实的直观理解。他的和平主义立场和公民权利活动使他成为知识分子的道德榜样。然而，历史学界也日益认识到爱因斯坦的复杂性，他既是革命性的思想家，也是特定历史条件下的产物，其科学成就和政治立场都需要放在20世纪动荡的历史背景中理解。
objective.en: In historical and popular culture contexts, Einstein has transcended his scientific field to become a cultural symbol. He is widely regarded as the embodiment of genius, with his image frequently representing wisdom and creativity. Einstein's theories of relativity are not only scientific achievements but also sources of philosophical thought, challenging intuitive understandings of time, space, and reality. His pacifist stance and civil rights activism have made him a moral exemplar for intellectuals. However, historians increasingly recognize Einstein's complexity—as both a revolutionary thinker and a product of specific historical circumstances—understanding that his scientific achievements and political positions must be contextualized within the turbulent history of the 20th century.

self.zh: 想象力比知识更重要，因为知识是有限的，而想象力概括着世界上的一切，推动着进步，并且是知识进化的源泉。
self.en: Imagination is more important than knowledge. For knowledge is limited, whereas imagination embraces the entire world, stimulating progress, giving birth to evolution.
